title: Why managed services beat raw AWS on real cost: free tiers, engineer time, and scale-to-zero
summary: Theo argues that "AWS is cheaper" claims miss three things: generous free tiers carry small projects a long way, engineer time is the biggest hidden cost, and managed services let you build in ways that cost less to run. His takeaway is that most teams self-hosting need a very good reason, because they are usually spending more.

principles.text: Generous free tiers on modern managed services carry most small projects far; check them before assuming you need raw cloud.
principles.quote: the free tier carries you really far

principles.text: Engineer time is the real cost of DIY infrastructure; setup and maintenance hours dwarf small monthly savings.
principles.quote: we're talking hundreds upon hundreds of hours and whether or not I like to admit it that's expensive

principles.text: Spend engineering time on product differentiation, not on shaving the infrastructure bill.
principles.quote: your engineer should be spending time making your product better for your users so you can beat your competition not making your AWS cheaper

principles.text: Don't rewrite onto self-hosted infrastructure to cut cost until a service is stable and high-traffic; most teams are far from that point.
principles.quote: most of us are very far from that point even y'all working at big companies because most code is changing and the cost of change is high

principles.text: Usage-based, scale-to-zero billing aligns cost with traffic; running servers means paying for idle compute.
principles.quote: if you're running servers you're paying for a compute that isn't being used period

principles.text: Caching responses is far cheaper than computing every request; invalidate only on real changes.
principles.quote: it's so much cheaper to Cache a response than to run a server that processes every single request like comically
